The '''2011–12 Football League Cup''' (known as the '''Carling Cup''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 52nd season of the [[EFL Cup|Football League Cup]], a knock-out competition for the top 92 [[Association football|football]] clubs played in [[English football league system]]. [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] were the [[2011 Football League Cup Final|defending champions]], but were knocked out 2–0 by [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the Third Round.

[[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], the winner of the competition, qualified for the [[2012–13 UEFA Europa League#Third qualifying round|third qualifying round]] of the [[2012–13 UEFA Europa League]]. The [[2012 Football League Cup Final|final]] was held on 26 February 2012, and was contested at [[Wembley Stadium]] between finalists [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] and [[Cardiff City]]. Cardiff were the first team outside the Premier League to appear in a League Cup final since 2001. It was Liverpool's first appearance at the new Wembley. Liverpool won the final 3–2 on penalties, claiming a record eighth League Cup, after the score was 2–2 after extra time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/fa-league-cups/liverpool-class-finally-tells-to-deny-mackays-battlers-7441243.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220501/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/fa-league-cups/liverpool-class-finally-tells-to-deny-mackays-battlers-7441243.html |archive-date=1 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live
|title=Liverpool class finally tells to deny Mackay's battlers |date=27 February 2012|work=The Independent|access-date=27 February 2012}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

==Background==

===Broadcasting rights===
The broadcasting rights for the 2011–12 Cup in the UK were shared between [[Sky Sports]] and the [[BBC]]. Sky Sports had rights to broadcast two live matches from each round while the BBC showed match highlights online and on a special League Cup highlights show which was broadcast in the late evening on BBC One.<ref>{{Cite news |title=BBC wins Football League contract |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/7080696.stm |work=BBC Sport |date=6 November 2007}}</ref>

The BBC showed two legs of the semi-final fixtures and Sky Sports showed the other two.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Football on the BBC – Football League |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/8170690.stm |work=BBC |access-date=23 August 2011 |date=2 August 2010}}</ref> Both BBC and Sky Sports simulcasted the final on 26 February 2012.

==Preliminary round==
''Times up to and including the fourth round are [[British Summer Time|BST]] ([[UTC+01:00|UTC+1]]). Times from the quarter-finals onwards are [[Greenwich Mean Time|GMT]] ([[UTC±0]]).''

Due to newly relegated (and League Cup title holders) [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] having a [[Bye (sports)|bye]] to the third round following qualification to the [[2011–12 UEFA Europa League#Play-off round|Europa League]] and the extra Europa League berth awarded to [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] through the Fair Play league, newly promoted [[AFC Wimbledon]] and [[Crawley Town F.C.|Crawley Town]] played each other in a preliminary round. The draw for the round took place on 13 June with Crawley Town at home. This was the first need for a Preliminary Round since the [[2002–03 Football League Cup|2002–03 season]].

==First round==
The draw for the first round took place on 16 June 2011 at 10:00 [[British Summer Time|BST]]. The First Round took place in the week commencing 8 August 2011. [[2011 England riots|Rioting in London]] caused three matches to be postponed on the advice of the [[Metropolitan Police]]. The fixtures at [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]], [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] and [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] were called off on safety grounds. The ties at [[Bristol City F.C.|Bristol City]] and [[Bristol Rovers F.C.|Bristol Rovers]] were called off later after the disorder spread across England.<ref>{{cite news |title=Charlton-Reading Carling Cup match called off |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14368434 |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=8 August 2011 |access-date=9 August 2011 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Crystal Palace v Crawley Town |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14368399 |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=8 August 2011 |access-date=9 August 2011 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=West Ham-Aldershot Carling Cup tie postponed on police advice |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14368510 |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=8 August 2011 |access-date=9 August 2011 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Bristol City-Swindon Carling Cup game called off |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14368515 |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=9 August 2011 |access-date=9 August 2011 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Bristol Rovers' Carling Cup tie with Watford postponed |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14383984 |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=10 August 2011 |access-date=10 August 2011 }}</ref> The round was also notable, from a footballing perspective, for the first competitive [[Nottingham derby]] since 1994 between [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] and rivals [[Notts County F.C.|Notts County]]. The match ended 3–3, with Forest winning the subsequent penalty shoot-out 4–3.

==Second round==
The draw for the second round took place on 11 August 2011. The thirteen [[2011–12 Premier League|Premier League]] teams not involved in European competition entered the competition at this stage.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.carling.com/carlingcup/draw/ |title=Carling Lager &#124; Refreshingly Perfect &#124; Carling.com |access-date=9 August 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130720040850/http://www.carling.com/ |archive-date=20 July 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

The second round took place in the week commencing 22 August 2011.

==Third round==
The draw for the third round took place on 27 August 2011. The eight [[English clubs in European football|English]] clubs who qualified for European competition in the [[2010–11 Premier League#League table|2010–11 season]] – [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]], [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]], [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] and [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] – entered the competition at this stage. Only two teams from [[2011–12 Football League Two|League Two]] remained at this stage: [[Aldershot Town F.C.|Aldershot Town]] and [[Shrewsbury Town F.C.|Shrewsbury Town]].

The Third Round took place in the week commencing 19 September 2011.

==Semi-finals==
The draw for the semi-finals took place on 30 November 2011. Unlike the rest of the tournament, the semi-finals are played over two legs, with the [[Aggregate score#Total points series (aggregate)|aggregate]] score after the second leg determining the winners. In the event of the aggregate scores being level after the second legs, 30 minutes of [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]] will be played, with the [[away goals rule]] applied.

The first legs took place in the week commencing 9 January 2012, with the second legs a fortnight later in the week commencing 23 January 2012.

==Final==
{{main|2012 Football League Cup Final}}
The final was played on 26 February 2012 at [[Wembley Stadium]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.carling.com/carlingcup/draw/ |title=Carling Lager &#124; Refreshingly Perfect &#124; Carling.com |access-date=9 August 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130720040850/http://www.carling.com/ |archive-date=20 July 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The final involved one team from the [[Premier League]], [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], and one from the [[Football League Championship|Championship]], [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]]. The game was won by Liverpool after a penalty shoot-out.
